description: Phytophthora blight is a destructive disease of cucurbit crops caused by the oomycete Phytophthora capsici. It infects seedlings, vines, leaves and fruits, often leading to rapid plant collapse and severe crop losses under warm and wet conditions.
symptoms: Seedling damping-off with water-soaked rot at soil line
Sudden wilting of plants without leaf yellowing
Water-soaked dark lesions on stems and vines
Leaf spots that become necrotic with olive or yellow borders
Fruit rot starting at the point touching the soil
White mold growth on rotting fruits
visual_symptoms: water-soaked lesions on stems and vines
white mold on infected cucurbit fruits
soft rotting pumpkins, cucumbers, or melons
sudden plant wilt and vine collapse
disease_cycle: Pathogen survives in soil as oospores for several years
Spores germinate and produce sporangia and zoospores
Zoospores swim in water and infect plant tissues
New spores form on infected plants and spread by water or rain
impact: Fruit rot in the field or storage
Rapid disease spread after heavy rain
Yield losses up to 100% in severe outbreaks
cultural_control: Use raised beds for cucurbit crops
Rotate fields with non-host crops for at least 3 years
Clean farm equipment before moving between fields
chemical_control: Seed treatment with mefenoxam or metalaxyl
Regular fungicide applications during wet conditions
prevention: Use clean fields without previous disease history
source: University of Illinois Plant Health Instructor
Babadoost M. 2005. Phytophthora blight of cucurbits
